result.summary: Do not ship: batches exceed the API cap, quota validation accepts invalid reserves, and the memory claim is contradicted by measurement. All five existing tests still pass.

findings.title: Batch size exceeds the 256-record API limit
findings.body: Both slicing and stepping use 265 instead of API_BATCH_LIMIT. make_batches(range(257)) returns one 257-record batch; 1,000 records produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. These violate the supplied API contract and cause upload rejection. Existing tests check counts without enforcing batch sizes.
findings.recommendation: Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for both slice width and stride. Test 256, 257, and multiple-batch inputs, asserting every batch is at most 256 records and flattening reproduces the input.

findings.title: Quota guard permits the forbidden boundary and NaN
findings.body: Three 30% shares leave exactly 10% by the quota contract, but floating-point arithmetic returns 0.10000000000000009 and accepts them. The existing test explicitly requires this incorrect acceptance. Also, [float('nan')] returns NaN because its <= comparison is false, despite failing the requirement that reserve be strictly above 10%.
findings.recommendation: Define quota precision and enforce the boundary using decimal or integer quota units; reject non-finite values explicitly. Replace the three-share acceptance test with rejection and add cases below, at, and above the threshold plus NaN.

findings.title: Documented memory profile is false for the implementation
findings.body: The docstring claims less than 4 MB for 10 million records because only one batch is retained. In fact, make_batches materializes the entire input and all output batches simultaneously. A tracemalloc run on Python 3.14.6 using repeat(None, 10000000) measured 162,424,168 peak bytes, even without allocating distinct record objects. Callers relying on the documented bound could exhaust memory.
findings.recommendation: Replace the claim with a reproducible measurement and document linear memory usage. If bounded memory is intended, implement lazy batching and measure incremental consumption before documenting that guarantee.

next_steps: Fix batching and quota validation, add boundary regression tests, and rerun unittest.
Correct the memory profile using a recorded benchmark workload and Python version.
